PullRequest.Title: build: restrict PR workflows to main and release branches
PullRequest.Body:
- restrict the chat-lib, telemetry, and Copilot setup workflows to PRs targeting `main` or `release/*`
- preserve the existing manual, push, and path-filter behavior
- align all active PR workflows on explicit base-branch filtering

Scenarios.Scenario: A pull request targets main or a release/* branch and triggers chat-lib tests.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: GitHub evaluates the base-branch filter before scheduling the three matrix jobs; once admitted, checkout, dependency setup, extraction, build, and tests are the CI critical path exactly as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Three OS-specific runners check out the repository and may restore/download npm packages before building and testing chat-lib.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three jobs per admitted pull_request event; each job performs one checkout and up to two npm dependency installations, with setup-node caches reducing package downloads on warm runs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same three jobs and boundary operations ran for every pull request regardless of base branch; the diff only suppresses runs for other base branches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations must finish for the chat-lib workflow check to complete.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One workflow run per qualifying pull_request event, multiplied by a fixed three-OS matrix; concurrency grouping coalesces superseded runs for the same PR via cancel-in-progress.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Up to three matrix jobs run concurrently per admitted event; the existing workflow-level concurrency group cancels an older run for the same pull request. The diff does not alter either behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: setup-node's npm cache is keyed by the two package lockfiles. Warm runs can avoid package downloads but still execute npm ci, extraction, build, and tests; branch filtering does not change keys or invalidation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed YAML is solely the pull_request branch predicate, while all jobs, matrix cardinality, cache configuration, and commands are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runner availability and cache-hit rates vary, but they affect only the unchanged cost of admitted runs.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. Main/release pull requests retain identical cost; other base branches now consume zero chat-lib runner work.

Scenarios.Scenario: A pull request targets main or release/* and runs the telemetry metadata check.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After GitHub admits the event, checkout, Node setup, and telemetry extraction must complete before this CI check finishes; nonmatching base branches no longer enter this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The runner checks out the repository, installs or resolves Node tooling, and npx fetches @vscode/telemetry-extractor when unavailable locally.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One job and one extractor invocation per admitted pull_request event; any package-manager caching is platform-managed and unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical job ran on pull requests to every base branch; after the diff it runs only for main and release/*.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The checkout/package resolution and full-source extractor invocation are serial steps on the workflow's completion path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The extractor scans the checked-out source tree for telemetry metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One repository-wide scan per admitted workflow run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The scan already occurred once on every pull_request workflow run; the branch filter only reduces the number of runs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The scan is the terminal substantive step and directly determines check latency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One workflow run per qualifying pull_request event, with extractor cost scaling with repository size rather than any new diff-controlled collection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No workflow concurrency group is defined, so distinct PR events may overlap as before; the new filter can only reduce the number admitted.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No explicit workflow cache is configured. Runner/npm incidental caching may vary, but the diff neither changes cache keys nor adds cold-cache work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the only changed behavior is event filtering before runner allocation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact package download and scan durations depend on runner state and repository size, but the admitted-run path is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. The change reduces possible network, filesystem, and CPU work and leaves eligible-run latency unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: The Copilot setup workflow is invoked by a matching workflow-file change, a push, or manual dispatch.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For pull requests, GitHub now evaluates both the existing path filter and the new base-branch filter before allocating the runner. For admitted PRs, pushes, and manual dispatches, system package setup, cache restoration, dependency installation on misses, and artifact downloads remain serial prerequisites to workflow completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: apt-get updates package indexes and installs system packages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One apt update/install sequence per admitted workflow run, with script-level retry behavior unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This sequence ran for every path-matching pull request plus the unchanged push/manual triggers; it now skips pull requests to other base branches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: System service setup blocks all later setup steps.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml, Restore node_modules cache and npm ci steps
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The workflow restores dependency caches and performs two npm ci installs on a cache miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cache restore per run and at most two npm installations per cold run, each with up to five attempts on failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cache keys, retry counts, and installation placement are unchanged; only fewer pull_request events are admitted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cache restoration or cold installation must complete before extension and runtime downloads.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml, built-in extension and Electron/Playwright download steps
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The workflow conditionally downloads built-in extensions and always invokes parallel Electron and Playwright download scripts, with up to three attempts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One built-in-extension download on a cache miss and one paired runtime-download invocation per run; retries occur only on failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same downloads and retry behavior existed on all triggers; the diff removes them only for non-main/non-release pull requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These downloads are the final prerequisites and block successful workflow completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One run per manual dispatch, matching push, or qualifying path-and-branch pull_request event; dependency volume controls bytes, while retries bound failed network attempts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Electron and Playwright downloads run as two parallel subprocesses within one step. Separate workflow runs have no explicit coalescing and may overlap as before; filtering decreases potential overlap from pull requests.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: node_modules cache uses a Linux/x64 architecture key and skips both npm ci steps on hits. Built-in extensions use a content hash and download only on misses. The filter does not alter cold/warm behavior, keys, or invalidation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: push and workflow_dispatch definitions are untouched, while the pull_request predicate is strictly narrower and all jobs are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold-cache frequency and network retry incidence are variable, but all costly paths are pre-existing and the diff only removes some invocations.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. Existing push/manual behavior and eligible PR cost are preserved; excluded PRs avoid substantial setup I/O.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the complete three-file diff. The added base-branch filters execute before workflow scheduling and strictly reduce CI invocations; they add no runner work, boundary calls, retained state, serialization, or concurrency. No reportable performance finding was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
